children: The co-chair of Willkie Farr & Gallagher's strategic capital and restructuring department, Debra Sinclair, is returning to her previous firm, Weil Gotshal & Manges.

Both Willkie and Weil have been undergoing leadership changes. Willkie recently brought in longtime Kirkland & Ellis partner Ryan Bennett to lead the firm's strategic capital and restructuring group. Weil elevated Matt Barr to global chair of its premier restructuring group, while private-equity attorney Ramona Nee is set to take over as the firm's executive partner.

"Debbie began her career at Weil and returns as an established leader in the restructuring market," Nee said. "That makes her return particularly meaningful for our firm and our people, and we are thrilled to welcome her home."

In addition to her role as department co-chair, Sinclair was also chair of Willkie's company restructuring and reorganization practice that specializes in representing chapter 11 debtors. Her notable assignments include leading the Saks Global bankruptcy restructuring, representing U.S. independent directors in the Cineworld chapter 11 case, and advising creditors to Remington Outdoor and Belk.

A 2013 graduate of New York University School of Law, Sinclair moved from Weil to Willkie in 2016, where she made partner and rose into a leadership role. Sinclair rejoins Weil as a partner in New York.

"Having started my career at Weil, I know firsthand the strength of the firm's premiere restructuring platform and the collaborative culture that sets the team apart," said Sinclair. "I am excited to return and build on my debtor-side practice alongside lawyers I have long respected, and to contribute to the continued growth of a team with such a strong reputation in the market."
